messages.subject: Re: Illogical results
parts:
It's difficult to tell what's going on here without knowing the content of the items, so I'm afraid we're at a loss for explaining this phenomenon (could be a method/wording effect, a missing causal factor resulting in even more multidimensionality, sampling error, etc). The surprising result is something worth looking into of course, it's just not clear what to do exactly without further information.

Phil


On Tue, Jan 23, 2024 at 8:46 AM ericami...@gmail.com <ericami...@gmail.com> wrote:
I have a hard time believing my MIRT-analysis results are correct. I have been assessing a questionnaire and recently added 1 new question (item1). The MIRT-results have so far been very logical and parallel to theoretical frameworks, but this new item doesn't behave as expected! 

In the first table are the pearson correlation scores. They are logical, item1 has high correlation with items logical1 and logical2, and low with "illogical" items. Yet in the table2 results of mirt, the item1 doesn't seem to go together with logical1 and logical2, and instead groups with illogical items. This feels highly unlikely and I cannot figure out what is going on. Could there be some issue? Or should I just accept the results as they are?

NOTE: there are more factors and items in the analysis, the tables are just to show the most confusing results.




Please any tips and comments are appreciated!


--
